parents.reason: Adapted Arabic writing supported the Persian manuscript tradition in which quatrains circulated.

title: Rap performance
summary: Performers organize rhythmic speech through rhyme, phrasing, and musical accompaniment.

parents.reason: Rhythmic accompaniment provides a temporal structure against which spoken lines are performed.

title: Reggae
summary: Jamaican musicians developed a distinctive rhythmic style with wide cultural circulation.

parents.reason: Jazz and related North American music contributed to the Jamaican musical mixtures preceding reggae.

title: Blues
summary: African American musicians developed expressive song traditions using recurring tonal and phrase conventions.

parents.reason: Work songs, spirituals, and other existing musical practices supplied performance resources reshaped into blues.

title: Rock and roll
summary: Musicians combined rhythm-and-blues, country, and other influences into a widely circulating popular style.

parents.reason: Blues-derived forms, phrasing, and rhythmic practices contributed to early rock-and-roll performance.

title: Gospel music
summary: Christian devotional music developed prominent African American performance and composition traditions.

parents.reason: Church worship and religious teaching provide settings and subjects for gospel performance.

title: Soul music
summary: African American musicians developed popular styles combining gospel expression with secular song traditions.

parents.reason: Vocal techniques and call-and-response practices from gospel contributed to soul performance.

title: Son cubano
summary: Cuban musicians combined African-derived rhythmic practices with Spanish-derived song and harmonic traditions.

parents.reason: Existing rhythmic, vocal, and ensemble practices supplied the materials combined in son.

title: Bossa nova
summary: Brazilian musicians developed an intimate song style reworking samba rhythm and harmonic language.

parents.reason: Samba's rhythmic organization supplied patterns transformed in bossa nova accompaniment and phrasing.

title: Flamenco
summary: Andalusian traditions combine song, instrumental accompaniment, and expressive dance.

parents.reason: Footwork and coordinated bodily expression contribute central rhythmic and dramatic elements.

title: Fado
summary: Portuguese performers cultivated urban song traditions associated with expressive narrative and feeling.

parents.reason: Vocal melody and accompaniment provide the expressive means through which fado narratives are presented.

title: Qawwali
summary: South Asian Sufi performance combines devotional poetry, singing, and coordinated musical response.

parents.reason: Sufi devotional settings and concepts supply the religious purposes and textual subjects of the performance.

title: Sikh kirtan
summary: Sikh communities sing sacred compositions as a central form of shared worship.

parents.reason: The gurus' compositions and communal worship practices supply the texts and setting for devotional singing.

title: Gregorian chant
summary: Western Christian communities organized a repertoire of monophonic liturgical singing.

parents.reason: Monastic prayer schedules and teaching communities supported the repeated performance and transmission of chants.

title: Polyphonic composition
summary: Composers organize simultaneous melodic lines into coordinated musical textures.

parents.reason: Liturgical chant supplied melodies around which early written multi-voice compositions were developed.

title: Fugue
summary: A contrapuntal composition develops a subject through imitative entries and related passages.

parents.reason: Coordinated independent voices supply the contrapuntal organization used in fugue.

title: Sonata form
summary: Composers organize large instrumental movements through contrasting and returning musical materials.

parents.reason: Established tonal and thematic practices supply material organized through the form.

title: Symphony
summary: Extended orchestral compositions coordinate multiple movements and instrumental groups.

parents.reason: Developing sonata procedures helped organize thematic contrast and return in symphonic movements.

title: Concerto
summary: Concertos organize musical interaction between featured performers and a larger ensemble.

parents.reason: Techniques for coordinating multiple musical parts support exchanges between solo and ensemble voices.

title: String quartet tradition
summary: Four-part string ensembles developed a major tradition of chamber composition and coordinated performance.

parents.reason: Independent but coordinated parts provide the compositional basis for four-player chamber works.

title: Staff musical notation
summary: Positioned marks on horizontal lines indicate pitches for repeatable musical reading.

parents.reason: The need to teach and transmit chant supplied an early practical setting for pitch-based staff notation.

title: Printed music publishing
summary: Printed scores distribute compositions to performers using repeatable written notation.

parents.reason: Press production allowed many copies of coordinated musical signs to reach performers.

title: Music conservatories
summary: Specialist institutions organize sustained training in musical performance and composition.

parents.reason: Supervised practical skill training supplied a model expanded through specialist courses and examinations.

title: Choral societies
summary: Voluntary singing organizations coordinate collective rehearsal and public vocal performance.

parents.reason: Accessible printed parts help groups learn and coordinate larger repertoires.

title: Modern Olympic Games
summary: An international movement established recurring athletic competition among national delegations.

parents.reason: The ancient festival supplied a historical model and name reinterpreted by modern organizers.

title: Codified cricket
summary: Written cricket laws standardize play and adjudication across clubs and matches.

parents.reason: Recorded rules give players and officials a shared reference for resolving disputes.

title: Codified rugby union
summary: Organized rugby institutions standardized a handling-based form of football.

parents.reason: Debates over competing football rules helped clarify the separate handling-based code formalized by rugby organizations.

title: Basketball
summary: James Naismith devised an indoor team game with written rules for coordinated competitive play.

parents.reason: Organized schooling and physical instruction supplied settings for teaching a new supervised team game.

title: Volleyball
summary: William Morgan devised a net-based team game emphasizing repeated exchanges between opposing sides.

parents.reason: Morgan sought a less strenuous alternative to basketball for participants in his physical-education program.

title: Judo
summary: Kanō Jigorō organized a martial training system around selected techniques and educational aims.

parents.reason: Extended supervised martial instruction supplied techniques and teaching relationships reorganized within the new system.

title: Karate training standardization
summary: Karate schools increasingly organized instruction through shared uniforms, ranks, and formal teaching systems.

parents.reason: Judo's uniforms and ranking practices provided models adopted in modern karate teaching.

title: Breaking
summary: Urban dancers developed competitive movement forms combining footwork, freezes, and acrobatic expression.

parents.reason: Social dance supplied the expressive practice developed into breaking's distinctive vocabulary.

title: Modern dance
summary: Choreographers developed theatrical movement traditions questioning inherited ballet conventions.

parents.reason: Ballet training and conventions supplied techniques and assumptions that modern choreographers adapted or challenged.

title: Bharatanatyam revival
summary: Performers and institutions reshaped a South Indian dance tradition into a prominent concert form.

parents.reason: Classical theories of expressive gesture and aesthetic response informed the dance's performance vocabulary.

title: Rule of Saint Benedict
summary: A written monastic rule organized communal prayer, work, discipline, and leadership.

parents.reason: Established monastic communities supplied the practical life and responsibilities addressed by the rule.

title: Cistercian Order
summary: A monastic order organized communities around a reform of Benedictine observance.

parents.reason: The Benedictine rule supplied the shared discipline the reformers sought to implement more strictly.

title: Franciscan Order
summary: Franciscan communities organized religious life around poverty, preaching, and service.

parents.reason: Earlier communal religious disciplines supplied practices adapted into a mendicant form of life.

title: Dominican Order
summary: A religious order coordinated preaching, study, and communal life.

parents.reason: Christian preaching and theological teaching supplied the order's purposes and institutional authorization.

title: Society of Jesus
summary: The Jesuit order developed coordinated religious, missionary, and educational activity.

parents.reason: Christian religious commitments and papal approval supplied its purposes and institutional basis.

title: Khalsa
summary: Guru Gobind Singh established an initiated Sikh community with shared commitments and public identity.

parents.reason: The existing Sikh community and teachings supplied the religious tradition organized through Khalsa initiation.

title: Sikh langar
summary: Communal kitchens provide shared meals open to participants without caste distinction.

parents.reason: Sikh teachings on equality and service supply the practice's purposes and community support.

title: Nizamiyya teaching institutions
summary: Patron-supported teaching institutions organized Sunni legal and theological education.

parents.reason: The existing madrasa form supplied the residential and teaching organization expanded through coordinated patronage.

title: Public primary education systems
summary: Public institutions increasingly organized and financed elementary schooling for broad populations.

parents.reason: Schooling requirements created responsibilities and demand for accessible elementary teaching.

title: School meal programs
summary: Organized feeding programs support pupils' access to nutrition during the school day.

parents.reason: Regular school attendance provides a continuing setting for reaching children through public meal provision.

title: School libraries
summary: Libraries within schools support reading, instruction, and learners' access to information.

parents.reason: Public-library collection and lending practices supplied models adapted to school learning.

title: Cuban Literacy Campaign
summary: A nationwide campaign mobilized instructors and learners to expand reading and writing skills.

parents.reason: Earlier large-scale literacy efforts supplied precedents for coordinated adult instruction.

title: Nonformal education programs
summary: Organized learning outside ordinary school structures addresses defined community and learner needs.

parents.reason: Adult learning initiatives demonstrated how structured instruction could operate outside childhood schooling.

title: Scouting
summary: Youth organizations developed shared programs of outdoor activity, service, and practical learning.

parents.reason: Learning by supervised practice supplied a method adapted to staged youth skill development.

title: Girl Guiding
summary: Guiding organizations adapted organized outdoor learning and service programs for girls.

parents.reason: Scouting activities and group structures supplied the model adapted by guiding organizations.

title: Credit-rating organizations
summary: Commercial agencies collect information and assess borrowers' ability to meet financial obligations.

parents.reason: Lending relationships create demand for information about repayment risk beyond personal acquaintance.

title: Statutory limited liability

parents.reason: Share-based corporate ownership supplied the investment structure to which liability limits were applied.

title: Statutory bankruptcy discharge
summary: English reforms allowed qualifying bankrupt debtors to obtain discharge under specified procedures.

parents.reason: Commercial debt and creditor procedures supplied the legal problems reorganized through statutory discharge.

title: Statute of Monopolies
summary: English legislation constrained monopolies while preserving specified privileges for new inventions.

parents.reason: Parliamentary lawmaking provided authority to revise the Crown's granting of monopoly privileges.

title: Statutory trademark registration
summary: Registration systems provide formal protection for signs identifying commercial sources.

parents.reason: Repeated exchange between unfamiliar buyers and suppliers creates demand for recognizable source identifiers.

title: Kitemark certification
summary: A standards organization's certification mark identifies products assessed against specified requirements.

parents.reason: Published common specifications provide criteria against which assessors can judge conformity.

title: British standards organization
summary: A national standards organization coordinated common specifications for industry.

parents.reason: Earlier standardization of quantities supplied a precedent for coordinating broader industrial specifications.

title: Educational accreditation
summary: Review organizations evaluate educational institutions or programs against agreed criteria.

parents.reason: Established institutions and qualifications create a need to compare the quality and recognition of educational provision.

title: Organized quality management
summary: Organizations coordinate procedures, improvement, and assessment to maintain desired quality.

parents.reason: Statistical assessment supplies methods for distinguishing process variation and evaluating improvement.

title: Modern occupational safety regulation
wiki: Occupational Safety and Health Act (United States)
summary: United States legislation established a coordinated federal framework for workplace safety and health.

parents.reason: Earlier international labor standards helped establish workplace protection as a public regulatory responsibility.

title: Organized disaster relief
summary: Relief organizations coordinate personnel, supplies, and assistance after major disasters.

parents.reason: An established humanitarian organization supplies trained volunteers and coordination structures adaptable to disasters.

title: Humanitarian logistics
summary: Relief operations coordinate purchasing, storage, transport, and distribution under crisis conditions.

parents.reason: General supply coordination provides methods adapted to urgent relief and disrupted infrastructure.

title: Prepaid adhesive postage
summary: Standardized stamps document advance payment for mail delivery.

parents.reason: Organized mail services provide routes and accounting systems in which prepaid postage can be recognized.

title: Registered mail

parents.reason: Managed delivery networks provide custody points at which valuable mail can be documented.

title: Parcel post
summary: Postal services organize delivery of packages through standardized public arrangements.

parents.reason: Existing routes and service administration provide a network extended to handling parcels.

title: Freight forwarding organizations
summary: Intermediaries arrange shipment and related services across carriers and jurisdictions.

parents.reason: Coordinated movement and storage practices provide the operational tasks assembled by forwarding firms.

title: Liner shipping conferences
summary: Shipping operators formed associations to coordinate specified services and commercial terms.

parents.reason: Scheduled steamship services created recurring capacity and pricing questions that operators coordinated.

title: Incoterms

parents.reason: The international commercial association coordinated publication of commonly interpreted trade terms.

title: International Chamber of Commerce
summary: An international business organization coordinates commercial rules, representation, and dispute services.

parents.reason: National and local commercial associations supplied a representation model extended across borders.

title: International Air Transport Association
summary: Airlines formed an association to coordinate commercial aviation practices and services.

parents.reason: Established airport networks made regular airline services possible across many destinations.

title: International Civil Aviation Organization
summary: An international organization coordinates civil aviation standards and cooperation.

parents.reason: Practical powered flight created international operations requiring common safety and navigation arrangements.

title: International Maritime Organization
summary: A specialized international organization coordinates maritime safety and related shipping rules.

parents.reason: The postwar UN system supplied a framework for establishing a specialized shipping organization.

title: Intermodal shipment documentation
summary: Coordinated documents describe consignments moving through multiple transport modes.

parents.reason: Standardized containers facilitate transfers whose custody and obligations can be tracked through combined documents.

title: International time-zone coordination
summary: Coordinated time conventions reduce ambiguity in schedules and communication between regions.

parents.reason: Long-distance rail timetables created practical demand for consistent time conventions across localities.

title: International Date Line convention

parents.reason: Coordinated global timekeeping creates a need to reconcile the calendar change around the world.

title: Postal codes
summary: Area codes assist postal sorting and routing within delivery networks.

parents.reason: Large managed delivery systems create repeated routing decisions that compact area identifiers can simplify.

title: Systematic addressing
summary: Organized place identifiers allow people, goods, and services to locate destinations reliably.

parents.reason: Dense streets and buildings create navigation and delivery needs beyond personal local knowledge.

title: Street numbering
summary: Assigned building numbers distinguish destinations along named streets.

parents.reason: Structured address conventions provide the framework in which building numbers identify individual destinations.

title: Postal money orders

parents.reason: A distributed office network provides local points for issuing and redeeming payment orders.

title: International reply coupons

parents.reason: The union's international congress agreed a coupon that participating national services could redeem for postage.

title: Correspondence chess

parents.reason: Reliable message delivery allows opponents in different places to exchange recorded moves.

title: Organized book clubs
summary: Membership organizations select and distribute books to recurring groups of readers.

parents.reason: Commercial editions and distribution networks provide books that membership services can select and deliver.

title: Cheltenham Literature Festival

parents.reason: Published works and author-reader networks supply the material and participants for organized literary events.

title: Mechanics' institutes
summary: Educational associations provided workers with lectures, libraries, and practical opportunities for learning.

parents.reason: Occupational skill learning supplied practical needs supplemented by workers' lectures and accessible educational collections.

title: Oral-history interviewing
summary: Researchers preserve interviews about remembered experience for later historical interpretation.

parents.reason: Spoken transmission of remembered events supplies a source tradition reorganized through deliberate interviews and archival preservation.

title: Community radio
summary: Locally governed broadcasters provide programming shaped by participating communities.

parents.reason: Radio transmission provides the distribution medium organized through local participation and governance.
